answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated, costly escrowed trades with distinct counterparties: each trade locks a small deposit, and disputes or failed delivery can slash it. A pulse of new accounts therefore cannot create trusted history cheaply; the attacker must fund many deposits and sustain believable exchanges with independently established agents. Reusing a tight lagoon of colluding identities is detectable through shared counterparties and settlement patterns, while a long thread of verified trades takes time and capital to build.
